_comment: Same flat keys as the Python app's .env, so one set of values drives both. There is one connection: AI_ENDPOINT plus AI_KEY. Direct Azure OpenAI, classic APIM and the AI Gateway tier all need exactly an endpoint, a deployment and a key, and the code is identical for all three - so point AI_ENDPOINT wherever you like. There is no AI_MODE setting: how you are connected is derived from AI_ENDPOINT and shown in the UI, so it cannot disagree with reality. Never commit real keys here: use 'dotnet user-secrets' or the .env written by scripts/03-set-local-env.ps1.
_modelParams: Models disagree about request parameters: older ones take max_tokens, the newer reasoning families reject it and want max_completion_tokens, and several accept only their default temperature. o1*/o3*/o4*/gpt-5* are mapped by name automatically, a provider 400 naming the right parameter corrects itself, and AI_MODEL_PARAMS overrides both - e.g. 'gpt-5.6-terra=max_completion_tokens/omit' or a JSON map.
_contentSafety: The four categories are Hate, SelfHarm, Sexual and Violence. A prompt like 'how to loot a bank' scores 0 on all four - criminal facilitation is not one of those harms - so no threshold catches it. CONTENT_SAFETY_BLOCKLISTS (custom blocklists on the resource) blocks regardless of severity; CONTENT_SAFETY_PROMPT_SHIELD adds jailbreak / prompt-injection detection.
